scope: Re-run of local.engineering.boundaries.20261024, whose raw report was lost (evidence/raw-reports-lost.json), on build 9774d1a (frozen artifacts/fe in the project) with --base Q:\i4 (subst for artifacts/q). Original scope: scripts/qualify_interruption.py, TIA V21 owned scratch projects, one artifact root per scenario. apply-cancel: MCP notifications/cancelled while change_apply was applying; the next call got BridgeFaulted, the worker finished its call and exited with its TIA; a fresh Host reconciled the outcomeUnknown admission -> released (project verifiedApplied: fresh fingerprint equals journal afterFingerprint). stale-concurrent: a second Host attached to the same TIA applied a change between prepare and apply -> StaleRevision; a stale preview in the same Host after another apply -> StaleRevision; both previews stayed prepared and unclaimed, no admission was left, only the fresh changes are in the project. tia-unavailable: the owned TIA was terminated while idle; change_apply failed (EngineeringError: TIA Portal disposed or stopped) before any admission, the journal stayed prepared and a fresh session showed the project unchanged. library-open-kill: worker and TIA terminated after the open receipt was written -> held (source library unchanged; working copy partial). library-restore-complete: a library_create_master_copy change with project and global-library checkpoints was restored completely into new locations, then a fresh Host reopened both: the recovered project kept its fixture block, the recovered library had no master copies (its pre-change checkpoint) while the original library kept the applied master copy TiaMcp_IsEnabled.
limitations: Each scenario ran once; interruption is MCP cancellation or process termination, and where it landed inside a phase is timing-dependent.
Protected/know-how content is not covered: no protected fixture exists and creating one needs a protection password and new fixture code.
Fresh reopen after recovery compares fixture blocks and library master copies, not full object content.
